newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel ally says defence must finance Eurofighter.
newsitem.headline: Waigel ally says defence must finance Eurofighter.

text.p: A top ally of German Finance Minister Theo Waigel warned the Defence Ministry on Sunday not to try to squeeze additional funds from the state to fund Germany's share of the four-nation Eurofighter aircraft project.
Waigel this week gave his support for German participation in the venture but did not go as far as actually pledging funds.

Michael Glos, parliamentary leader of Waigel's Christian Social Union (CSU), a member of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition, urged Defence Minister Volker Ruehe to make savings in his own budget to ensure Germany can finance its share of the fighter plane.
"Volker Ruehe should not go too far with his attempt to squeeze more money from the finance minister," he told the Bild am Sonntag weekly.

Eurofighter -- which is being jointly developed by Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA), British Aerospace, Spain's CASA and Italy's Alenia -- is expected to cost Germany alone a total of 23 billion marks.
Germany's struggle to close a gaping budget deficit gap and qualify for European monetary union has cast doubt on its ability or resolve to fund its planned purchase of 180 Eurofighter jets.
However, Ruehe has said he expects the funds to be approved after cabinet budget meetings next month.

He has also been quoted as saying he believes the overall defence budget will not be cut in the future, and that German participation in the scheme will be dependent on funds being redirected into Eurofighter that were initially advanced to DASA for other purposes.

DASA chief executive Manfred Bischoff said at the Paris airshow on Sunday he was confident the German government would approve funding to move the Eurofighter into production, but repeated a warning that DASA would stop pre-production work if the cabinet did not approve funding before the summer recess.
